explain.say: The Tao Te Ching is the central book of Taoism, a tradition from ancient China. Its title means the classic of the Way and its power, and it has just 81 short chapters, about 5,000 Chinese characters.

draw.text: Tao: the Way. Te: its power, or virtue. Ching: classic

explain.say: It is traditionally said to be by Laozi, the old master. A legend says he was leaving China for the west when a gatekeeper asked him to write down his wisdom, and he left this little book behind.

items: He sets out for the west
A gatekeeper asks him to write

draw.text: The legend is told by the historian Sima Qian, about 100 BCE

explain.say: The book begins by saying that the Tao which can be put into words is not the eternal Tao. The Tao is the natural way of everything, the source of all things, which can be followed but never fully named.

draw.value: The Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao. The name that can be named is not the eternal name.
draw.label: Tao Te Ching, chapter 1, a common rendering

draw.text: The Tao: the Way of nature, beyond words

explain.say: Water is the book's favourite picture. Water is soft and humble and flows to the lowest places, yet it helps all living things and, in time, wears away the hardest stone.

items: Soft: yet it wears away stone
Still: muddy water clears when calm

draw.text: Chapter 8: the highest good is like water

explain.say: A key idea is wu wei, acting without forcing, like a river flowing round a rock. The book also sees opposites, like soft and hard or dark and light, as partners in balance, the idea pictured by yin and yang.

draw.text: Wu wei: effortless action, going with the flow
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step: chapter 64

explain.say: Tradition places Laozi in the 6th century BCE, but many scholars think the book was gathered over time and took shape around the 4th century BCE. Today it is one of the most translated books in the world.

items: Many scholars: compiled about 4th century BCE
About 300 BCE: Guodian bamboo slips, oldest copies
Today: one of the most translated books

draw.text: Two parts: the Tao, chapters 1 to 37, and the Te, 38 to 81

faq.q: What does the Tao Te Ching teach?
faq.a: It teaches living in harmony with the Tao, the natural Way of the universe. It praises simplicity, humility, gentleness and wu wei, acting without forcing, and it often uses water as its example.
asks: What is the main message of the Tao Te Ching?
What are the teachings of Taoism?
What does the Daodejing say?

faq.q: Who wrote the Tao Te Ching?
faq.a: Tradition says it was written by Laozi, whose name means old master, a keeper of archives at the Zhou royal court. Many scholars think it was gathered from the sayings of several people over time.
asks: Who is Laozi?
Who is Lao Tzu?
Was Laozi a real person?

faq.q: What does Tao Te Ching mean?
faq.a: Tao means the Way, Te means virtue or power, and Ching means classic or book. So the title is the classic of the Way and its power.
asks: What does Tao mean?
What does the title Tao Te Ching mean?
What is the Daodejing?

faq.q: How many chapters are in the Tao Te Ching?
faq.a: It has 81 short chapters, often only a few lines each, about 5,000 Chinese characters in all. It is divided into two parts: chapters 1 to 37 on the Tao, and 38 to 81 on Te.
asks: How long is the Tao Te Ching?
How many verses does the Tao Te Ching have?
Is the Tao Te Ching a short book?

faq.a: The Tao is the Way: the natural source and flow of everything in the universe. The book says it cannot be fully captured in words, but it can be followed by living simply and in harmony with nature.
asks: What is the Way in Taoism?
What does the Tao that can be told mean?
Is the Tao a god?

faq.q: Why does the Tao Te Ching talk about water?
faq.a: Water is its favourite example of the Tao. Water is soft and humble and flows to low places, yet it nourishes everything and can wear away hard stone, showing that gentleness can be stronger than force.
asks: What does be like water mean?
What is the water metaphor in Taoism?
Why is water a symbol of the Tao?

faq.a: Wu wei means non-forcing or effortless action. It does not mean doing nothing; it means acting naturally and at the right time, without struggling against the flow of things, like water going round a rock.
asks: What does wu wei mean?
Does wu wei mean doing nothing?
What is effortless action?

faq.q: What is the legend of Laozi and the gatekeeper?
faq.a: The historian Sima Qian tells that Laozi, tired of the court, travelled west. At the border pass a gatekeeper begged him to write down his wisdom, so Laozi wrote a book of about 5,000 characters and then disappeared.
asks: How was the Tao Te Ching written?
Where did Laozi go?
Why did Laozi write the Tao Te Ching?

faq.q: How old is the Tao Te Ching?
faq.a: Tradition places Laozi in the 6th century BCE. Many scholars think the text took shape around the 4th century BCE; the oldest known copies, on bamboo slips from a tomb at Guodian, date from about 300 BCE.
asks: When was the Tao Te Ching written?
What is the oldest copy of the Tao Te Ching?
What are the Guodian slips?

faq.q: What is the most famous line of the Tao Te Ching?
faq.a: Two of the most famous are the opening, the Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao, and from chapter 64, a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
asks: Is a journey of a thousand miles from the Tao Te Ching?
What are famous Tao Te Ching quotes?
How does the Tao Te Ching begin?

faq.q: What is the connection between the Tao Te Ching and yin and yang?
faq.a: The Tao Te Ching often pairs opposites, like soft and hard, empty and full, as parts of one whole that need each other. This idea of balance is pictured in the yin and yang symbol, which became central to Taoist thought.
asks: Is yin and yang in the Tao Te Ching?
What does the Tao Te Ching say about opposites?
What is balance in Taoism?

faq.q: Is the Tao Te Ching a religious book or a philosophy book?
faq.a: Both. It is a classic of Chinese philosophy read by people of every background, and it is also the central scripture of the Taoist religion, where Laozi is honoured as a sage and a divine figure.
asks: Is Taoism a religion?
Do Taoists worship Laozi?
Is the Tao Te Ching scripture?

faq.q: What does the Tao Te Ching say about leaders?
faq.a: It says the best leaders are hardly noticed: when their work is done, the people say we did it ourselves. It warns against too many laws, war and showing off, and favours ruling gently and simply.
asks: What kind of ruler does the Tao Te Ching praise?
What does Laozi say about government?
What is a good leader in Taoism?

facts: The Tao Te Ching has 81 short chapters, about 5,000 Chinese characters.
The Tao Te Ching is traditionally attributed to Laozi, whose name means old master.
The oldest known copies of the Tao Te Ching are bamboo slips from a tomb at Guodian, from about 300 BCE.
Silk copies of the Tao Te Ching were found in a tomb at Mawangdui closed in 168 BCE.
The saying a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step comes from chapter 64 of the Tao Te Ching.

quiz.say: How many chapters does the Tao Te Ching have?
quiz.show: How many chapters are in the Tao Te Ching?
quiz.why: The Tao Te Ching has 81 short chapters, often only a few lines each.

wrong.0: 18 is the number of chapters in the Bhagavad Gita.
wrong.2: 114 is the number of surahs in the Quran.
wrong.3: 423 is the number of verses in the Buddhist Dhammapada.

quiz.say: A student is stuck on a hard problem. Instead of forcing it, she takes a calm break and the answer comes naturally. Which Taoist idea is this like?
quiz.show: Solving a problem by not forcing it is like which idea?
quiz.why: Wu wei means acting naturally without struggling, like water finding its way round a rock.

wrong.1: Pushing harder and harder is the forcing that the Tao Te Ching warns against.
wrong.2: Wu wei is not giving up; it is acting at the right time, in the right way.

quiz.say: The Tao Te Ching says nothing is softer than water, yet nothing is better at wearing down what is hard. What lesson does this teach?
quiz.show: Soft water wears away hard stone. What is the lesson?

options.say: Gentleness and patience can overcome force

quiz.why: Water shows that soft, patient, humble things can in time overcome the hard and strong, a central Taoist idea.

wrong.1: The book praises water as helpful to all things, not as a danger.
wrong.2: Stone is hard; the point is that softness wins over time, not that stone is weak.
